result.title: Effective Resistance and Graph Neural Network Reliability in Tissue-Specific Interactomes
result.summary: Protein function annotation needs to know which predictions to distrust, not only what a model predicts. We ask whether tissue-specific interaction structure carries that information. Our candidate signal is effective resistance, used previously to relieve over-squashing by rewiring. Across 24 tissue-specific interactomes it is dominated by inverse degree, and the degeneration deepens as the co-expression filtered network grows, with a Spearman correlation of -0.955. The residual departure from that limit exceeds degree-preserving null graphs in all 24 networks. Controlling for predictive entropy, degree, annotation cardinality, local structure and feature-only difficulty, the residual explains additional per-node loss in 19 of 24 held-out networks once a permutation floor is subtracted, at every depth, and the effect strengthens monotonically with depth. The increment reaches 0.37% of the variance the controls leave unexplained, 5.6 times a permutation floor, against 1.5 times when the model is retrained in a degree-preserving null world. Selective prediction improves negligibly. The signal is reproducible; degree degeneration bounds it.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究组织特异性蛋白互作网络中有效电阻（effective resistance）是否携带「哪些节点预测不可信」的信号，发现其被 inverse degree 主导且随网络增长而退化，残余部分在多数留出网络中可解释额外的逐节点损失。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但「有效电阻度量节点/结构可靠性并用于选择性预测」这一问题表述，可能启发 latent 推理中的证据筛选、中止决策与表示几何稳健性评估；度退化现象可供核查 latent 相似度是否被浅层统计量主导。
